notes: Silhouette IoU 0.723 against the star-free reference (0.198 at first render). Aspect delta 0.047 and scale delta 0.055 now PASS their Tier 1 thresholds (0.05/0.08); IoU does not (0.85). The residual is dominated by one thing, and it is not a fixable modelling error: the reference is not a consistent perspective projection. Matching its silhouette aspect requires a 16-degree camera pitch (solved by sweep), but at 16 degrees a wing of half-span 2.7 projects its far edge to Y=0.94 while the drawing puts the dorsal surface at Y=0.56 there. Satisfying that needs half-span 1.31 - and the measured span sweep shows narrower wings score WORSE overall (1.8 -> IoU 0.597 vs 2.7 -> 0.631), because they lose more overlap at the bow and tips than they gain above the wing root. The drawing shows more of the deck than any real camera at that aspect can. Remaining genuine geometry deltas, in size order: reference carries ventral mass under the stern bay that the model lacks; the model's bow wing tip sits low and short of the reference's; the tail blade is slightly oversized.

Reads as the reference's mechanism: tapered blade on measured proportions, open machinery face between leading and trailing spars, twin gold pivot bosses at the root, base housing with vents. Pivots on its hinge in the shipped viewer through the spec's -84..0 degree constraint. The exposed internals are present but read small at the review camera distance.

Strongest matched subsystem. Seven capsule pods in two staggered rows with 14 banding straps and the plumbing manifold, slung below the cradle shelf, bulging to the reference's measured ventral line. The soft-against-hard read that makes the reference recognisable is present, and the pods detach on the jettison control. Colour matches the sampled #e9b708 / #ae8100 pair.
